title: Specializing General-purpose LLM Embeddings for Implicit Hate Speech Detection across Datasets

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating implicit hate speech detection on benchmark datasets (such as IHC and ToxiGen) and specifically analyzing the model's sensitivity by comparing predicted hate probabilities for template statements substituting specific racial targets (e.g., 'Black people are stupid' vs. 'White people are stupid').

Evaluating implicit hate speech detection on benchmark datasets and explicitly analyzing target bias by comparing the classifier's predicted hate probabilities for template statements targeting religious groups (e.g., 'Jews are stupid' vs. 'Muslims are stupid').

Evaluating implicit hate speech detection on benchmark datasets and analyzing model sensitivity by measuring predicted hate probabilities for template statements targeting sexual minorities (e.g., 'Gay are stupid').

Benchmarking embedding models across diverse datasets (IHC, SBIC, DynaHate, ToxiGen) that contain implicit stereotypes, microaggressions, and coded hate speech targeting various marginalized demographic groups (including gender, nationality, and socioeconomic status).
